 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Primary consumers** typically occupy the second trophic level as they feed on autotrophs (plants).
 
• **Autotrophs** form the first trophic level since they produce their own food through photosynthesis or chemosynthesis.
 
• **Small carnivores** generally occupy the third trophic level as they prey on herbivores.
 
• **Bacteria** are not typically classified into a specific trophic level such as the fourth; they can be decomposers or participate in various trophic levels depending on the ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Producers (Autotrophs)**

 
 
• They are the base of the food chain and create organic material from inorganic substances.
 
• Examples include plants, algae, and some bacteria.
 
 
 
• **Primary Consumers (Herbivores)**
 
 
• They directly consume autotrophs.
 
• Examples include insects, deer, and rabbits.
 
 
 
• **Secondary and Tertiary Consumers (Carnivores)**
 
 
• They feed on herbivores and other carnivores.
 
• Examples include wolves, lions, and eagles.
